column1: # package-sizes-windows.tsv: measured seconds on windows-latest, the hosted image
# both Windows legs run on — test-windows-pr on a pull request and
# test-hosted-merge's windows leg on a merge group. Three tab-separated columns:
# `short` is `go test -short`, what the PR leg runs. `full` is `go test` with no
# -short, what the merge group runs. They are separate columns because they are
# separate measurements: the packages that dominate this table are exactly the
# ones whose heavy cases are gated behind testing.Short().
# A "-" is NOT MEASURED. A trailing "+" is CENSORED — the run hit its timeout, so
# the true size is AT LEAST that number and unknown above it. Both plans treat
# either one as "deal this package across every slot the group opened", because
# an unknown size must never be guessed downward.
# EVERY -short ROW IS NOW A REAL NUMBER, and that matters more than it sounds.
# The first version of this table had four censored rows at the 100 s ceiling and
# nothing else; every other package was unmeasured, so the plan dealt each of
# them across all three shards, paying a `go test -list` compile per package per
# shard for packages that turned out to take a tenth of a second. Run 35352593117
# replaced the guesses with measurements — and two of the four censored rows came
# back far smaller than their censoring suggested (cmd/nova-review 100.1+ is
# really 38.6 s, and it now runs whole in one slot) while two came back far
# larger (cmd/nova-merge 203.9 s, cmd/nova-bus 185.9 s). A censored row is not a
# conservative estimate; it is no estimate at all.
# THE LINUX TABLE CANNOT PREDICT THIS ONE, which is why this file exists instead
# of a multiplier over package-sizes.tsv. cmd/nova-bus is 10.0 s on an idle-ish
# hulk and 185.9 s here; cmd/nova-swarm is 51.0 s there and 18.4 s here. The
# difference is processes: the git-fixture packages spawn one per case and
# Windows pays the most per process, while nova-swarm's heavy cases skip under
# -short. The merge group deals its WINDOWS shards from this file; its linux and
# darwin legs keep reading package-sizes.tsv, which is their measurement.
# A NOTE ON HOW THE -short COLUMN WAS READ. Run 35352593117 dealt each of these
# packages across three shards, so the number here is the SUM of the three `ok`
# times for that package — the whole package's work, which is what the shard plan
# divides. A package that ran whole in one slot contributes that one number.
# The dealing is by test-name index, not by time, so the shares are uneven:
# cmd/nova-bus came back 40.7 + 46.5 + 98.7, a worst shard 1.6x the mean. The
# plan's budget and the leg's timeout both carry room for that.
# Measurements:
#   short: run 35352593117 (PR #1332, integration-4), 2026-09-18, windows-latest,
#          `go test -short -count=1 -timeout 180s`, whole tree (a go.mod change),
#          three shards. The run was CANCELLED by the job's six-minute cap — but
#          every shard had finished its last package two to four seconds before
#          against kills at 13:56:38-40), so the per-package times below are
#          complete and the only thing lost was the cleanup. That near miss is
#          the measurement the new cap is set from.
#   full:  the same PR's merge group, 2026-09-18. The windows leg's shard 0 of 3
#          for cmd/nova-bus was killed at the 100 s ceiling with
#          TestALanesReadmeIsNotANote, TestLaneStateFilesAreNotStrays and
#          TestTheCursorIsPushedLikeAReceipt still running. ONE THIRD of that
#          package exceeded 100 s, so the whole is far above it; 100.0+ is what
#          was actually observed and the "+" carries the rest.
# Four packages measured by that run are NOT in this tree — internal/dogfood,
# internal/friends, internal/goenv and internal/release arrived on the branch
# the run was testing. Their rows are left out rather than carried: this table
# is checked against the tree (internal/ci), so a row for a package that is not
# here is a row nobody can correct. They come back with the packages.
